As the new school year kicks off, more Americans now support keeping students entirely off their phones for the full school day.

The new school year has begun, and support for banning phones in classrooms continues to rise

That's right, it's still July, but summer vacation has somehow already come to an end. My own kids are heading back to school today and tomorrow — this is now the second summer in a row where the school year didn't start in August.

Apple is welcoming the new school year with its annual Back to School promotion, offering eligible students and educators up to US$150 in gift cards when they purchase select Mac and iPad products. The offer runs through August 27. Consumers in several states can also take advantage of limited sales tax holiday deals.

While back-to-school discounts are a welcome sight, the use of smartphones during school hours is increasingly falling out of favour.

Top-rated comment by GreenPizza

I've never seen any data to support the idea that letting students use their phones during school shooting events reduces risk. The reality is that classroom distractions have decreased, which aligns perfectly with the fundamental goal of going to school to learn.

A new survey from the Pew Research Center found that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using phones during class. That figure is up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025. Just 18% now oppose classroom bans.

Support for the stricter "bell-to-bell" ban has risen even more sharply. For the first time, more Americans support than oppose a total ban on phone use for the entire school day.

The report also notes that younger adults remain less supportive of both classroom and all-day bans, although support has risen across every age group since 2024. You can read the full report here.

What do you think? Should schools limit iPhone use to class periods only, enforce a bell-to-bell ban, or leave the decision to students and parents? Drop your thoughts in the comments.
